dedupe_keys.name: supplytwin open source supply chain digital twin for disruption scenarios

description: SupplyTwin is an interactive open-source digital twin for supply chain scenario simulation, released under Apache 2.0. The README describes a deterministic simulation in which users change demand, capacity, sourcing, inventory policy or transportation and follow the effects through suppliers, plants, distribution centres and customers, comparing a baseline with a disruption; an optional local AI translates scenario instructions and explains results, while the simulation computes every indicator. Its reference scenario removes 80% of one assembly plant's capacity for days 10 to 34 of a 60-day run on an included synthetic network: backlog exceeds the baseline on day 19, peaks at about 2,669 units on day 39 and clears on day 50, and the same-day fill rate falls from 99.96% to 94.37%. Coverage: user-defined networks, with a synthetic demo. Format and access: a web workspace run locally or with Docker Compose. Licence and cost: Apache 2.0, free, with no paid API needed. Caveats: the README calls it a v0.1.0 local release candidate, with Docker and hosted CI unverified, and results come from synthetic data. It supports digital twin, resilience and network flow studies of supply chain disruptions. It relates to the OFacT factory twin and the supply chain disruption monitoring dataset in the catalogue.
